conservation.condition_narrative:
Before the painting was purchased for the West Texas Museum Association in 1960, Caroline Kleck performed conservation work on the painting. "Sprayed with polybutyl methacrylate spray soluable in xylene and petroleum benzine October 1958 Caroline Keck." (black ink, original backing) "267-86" (Label, Texas Conservation Center) 
(Source: writing on board on back of painting, Catalogue Raissone by Barbara Buhler Lynes) 
In 1983 an Associate Conservator at the Kimbell Art Museum, Helen Mar Parkin, came to the Museum of Texas Tech to evaluate nine paintings. She wrote in her examination of this painting, "See conservator's written report. Condition stable. Needs inpainting, reframing. Conservator recommended painting be left off view until restored. STS". 
(Source: Examination Reports from Kimbell Art Museum, no further documentation) 
In 1987, Red Hills Series II-35 went to The Texas Conservation Center Panhandle-Plains Historical Museum, with Conservation File No.: 267-86. 
(Source: label on backing board and The Museum of Texas Tech University Artifact Activity Record Log; no further documentation) 
In 1988, the painting was re-framed at Charles Adams Gallery in Lubbock, TX to have UV plexiglass. 
(Source: The Museum of Texas Tech University Artifact Activity Record Log)

Stretcher: No inscriptions or marks. 
Original Backing: 
1.   “Bottom N.E” and “III” written in pencil; top left. 
2.   Gallery label from The Downtown Gallery; top left. 
3.   Notes from Caroline Keck, “Sprayed with polybutyl methacrylate spray soluble in xylene and petroleum benzine October 1958 Caroline Keck”; top left. 
4.   “Red Hills Series II-35" and “OK” written in a circle, written in graphite; center right. 
Museum at Texas Tech University, New Backing: 
1.   Gallery label from The Downtown Gallery; top left. 
2.   “RED HILLS SERIES II-35" written in pen; top center. 
3.   Museum at Texas Tech University Accession label; lower center. 
4.   Conservation label from The Texas Conservation Center Panhandle-Plains Historical Museum; lower center. 
5.   Object number label from The Texas Conservation Center Panhandle-Plains Historical Museum, “267-86”; center left. 
6.   “#54635” written in black crayon; center left. 
(Source: Museum at Texas Tech, 2025)
